questions.question: Explain why salt was so valuable in West Africa and where it came from.
questions.expected_answer: People in hot West Africa lose salt through sweat and needed it for health; salt also preserved meat and fish and kept livestock healthy. West Africa had little salt. It came from desert mines such as Taghaza and later Taoudenni, where deposits from ancient dried lakes were cut into slabs and carried south by camel; the long, dangerous journey raised its price.

questions.question: List three goods that went north and three that came south in the trans-Saharan trade.
questions.expected_answer: North: gold, ivory, ostrich feathers, kola nuts, enslaved people, hides. South: salt, cloth, copper, horses, glass beads, swords, paper and books, cowrie shells.

questions.question: Explain why a balanced history of the trans-Saharan trade must include the trade in enslaved people, and give one difference from the transatlantic slave trade.
questions.expected_answer: The trade brought wealth and learning to West African kingdoms and cities but also involved the capture and sale of millions of people over centuries, who suffered and many died; leaving them out gives a one-sided picture. Difference: it lasted far longer with smaller numbers each year, and enslaved people could sometimes gain freedom and rise in society.
